primary_object_card.object_statement: RELATIVE-ENTROPY-REF is the family of numeric quantum relative-entropy readouts D(rho_row||sigma_ref) on the same 18 declared row states, where every variant declares one fixed full-rank reference state and whether that reference can distinguish the row phase orientation; the family reports values and induced edge signs only.
primary_object_card.plain_language_definition: Each variant compares the same eighteen row density operators with one explicitly declared reference density operator. Changing the reference creates a new variant. References invariant to the row phase orientation must not distinguish orientation-paired rows; references with a transverse component may distinguish only the pairs whose density operators actually differ.

source_anchors.quote_or_summary: The frozen surface supplies the eighteen fixture observation rows used by every candidate family.
The demand surface supplies four ordered edge families totaling 169 edges, including nine orientation_winding pairs.
The incumbent fixes the exact behavior_v1.json schema and three-engine plus comparison-only layout.

native_terms.row state: The pure qubit density operator from |psi_row> = cos(a)|0> + orientation*sin(a)|1> for one frozen surface row.
native_terms.declared reference: A fixed full-rank qubit density operator whose Bloch vector, eigenvalues, phase, and regularization are recorded in variant parameters.
native_terms.phase blind: A reference with no transverse component relative to these real row states, so orientation-paired rows have identical relative entropy.
native_terms.phase breaking: A reference with a nonzero x component, so non-endpoint orientation-paired density operators can have different relative entropy.

weirdness_signature: phase sensitivity belongs to the declared reference rather than an added gate or label
literal rank-one references are excluded from the numeric grid because support mismatch makes relative entropy infinite
the endpoint orientation labels can differ while their density operators remain identical
primary_object_card.domain: the exact eighteen fixture rows and eleven declared full-rank qubit reference variants
primary_object_card.codomain_or_output: finite relative-entropy values for each row plus three-engine induced signs on all 169 demanded edges
allowed_operations: construct row density operators from frozen a and orientation fields
construct one full-rank reference density operator from declared variant parameters
evaluate quantum relative entropy with Hermitian eigendecompositions
compare Julia, JAX x64, and Torch f64 values
compute induced edge signs with the declared zero tolerance
required_invariants: all variants use the same eighteen rows in row_id order
each variant declares every reference-state parameter
each reference is positive definite and trace one
phase-blind references return zero signs on every orientation_winding edge
no candidate-lane logic adjudicates a demand or rung
forbidden_substitutions: marginal von Neumann entropy in place of relative entropy
clipped logarithm presented as literal pure-reference relative entropy
orientation label added directly to the scalar
gate outcome or L6 admission inferred from the behavior packet
negative_controls: maximally mixed reference is phase blind
z-axis near-pure references are phase blind on orientation pairs
erase the transverse reference component and require all orientation signs to become zero
compare endpoint orientation pairs whose density operators are identical
primary_object_card.adapter_policy: QuantumOptics, JAX, Torch, and NumPy are typed computation substrates. They may compute the declared family but may not redefine its rows, references, edge order, or claim ceiling.
promotion_locks: no L6 rung decision in the candidate directory
no literal pure-reference wording for regularized full-rank references
no scientific confirmation from cross-engine numeric agreement
primary_object_card.artifact_surface: append-only candidate directory with source, raw leg outputs, behavior_v1.json, receipt_v1.json, and deterministic rerun verification

root_constraints: finite eighteen-row carrier and finite reference grid
probe-relative distinguishability on the declared 169 edges
phase-sensitive and phase-blind references remain explicitly separated

loop_contract.repair_rule: repair the first schema, support, phase-symmetry, or determinism defect before adding variants
loop_contract.stop_condition: behavior and receipt rerun byte-identically with all engine legs complete, or a named runtime is blocked

method_contracts.question_is_not_authorization: A question asks for an answer; it is not authorization to implement unless the user explicitly says to do it.
method_contracts.order_check_separate: Any sequence or ordering claim must be checked separately from content correctness, with the order witness named.
method_contracts.baseline_preservation: When debugging runtime behavior, preserve the tuned visible/output baseline and debug the execution path underneath.
method_contracts.falsifier_first: A Popper pass names the target claim, strongest live falsifier, decisive check, and killed/open/survived classification before agreement.
method_contracts.feynman_testability: A Feynman pass names the operation, the observable measured, and the pass/fail condition.
method_contracts.synthesis_refusal: Synthesis must name distinct receipts and explicitly refuse the merge, sequence, or reframe it is not performing.
method_contracts.human_offload: Resolve with tools before asking; ask the human only for private, preference-bound, or unrecoverable information.
